QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_10

question.text: The Code of Conduct for SIAs lists a 'Non-Judgmental attitude' as the first core value. Which statement best captures what it requires of the SIA during an assessment?

answer.text: Avoid reaching any opinion at all — including the final signed opinion
Rely solely on documentary evidence and refuse beneficiary interviews that may trigger emotional judgement
Allow the SE's view to always prevail where evidence is ambiguous
Plan and perform the assessment without preconceived notions, so as to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence of program implementation with objectivity, fairness and accuracy

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 5.3.2 states: 'The Social Impact Assessor should plan and perform a social impact assessment with a non-judgmental attitude to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence of the implementation of the social program in the field. Maintaining a non-judgmental attitude during a social impact assessment is crucial for ensuring objectivity, fairness, and accuracy.' The Trap: A confuses non-judgmental attitude with not issuing any opinion — the SIA MUST issue an opinion/conclusion. C treats non-judgemental as pro-SE bias, which would violate objectivity. B misreads the principle — beneficiary interviews are central to evidence. Cross-Exam Context: NISM X-A / X-B (IA) Code of Conduct uses 'fairness to client'; XXIII specifies fairness to program, community, and evidence, not only to the engaging party. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Structure every interview with a factual opener and reserve interpretation for the working-paper analysis — this discipline keeps the non-judgemental tone intact even when beneficiary stories are emotionally charged.
